name: splash court: all 10 players get random rarity-weighted abilities, and the ability-only animations actually fire in the attract loop
description: ABILITIES_PER_PLAYER in SplashCourt.jsx rolls N distinct abilities for every player on both fixture rosters via rollAbilities() in abilityRoll.js. Two things are checked. (1) DETERMINISTIC: every one of the 10 splash-player nodes exposes data-abilities with exactly 2 distinct names, so nobody was missed and nothing duplicated - the whole point of the change is that the sim otherwise only ever plays run/shoot/block/idle. (2) BEHAVIOURAL: sample data-anim until an ability-GATED animation appears (spindunk/ironblock/pickpocket/fadeaway/spin/dash). None of those six can occur without an ability, so seeing one proves useGame's hasAbility() is really reading the roster rows this component builds. Runs in App Desktop/Mobile: the splash normally only mounts inline (real feed or Post View), and Post View is not a WebContentsView, so step 1 navigates to ?mode=inline - App.jsx's DEV-only mode override.

steps._comment: Post View is not a WebContentsView so the runner cannot attach to it. App.jsx's getMode() honours ?mode=inline in DEV builds, which mounts the same inline branch (SplashCourt) inside a normal webview. The cache-busting t= also guarantees a fresh module load, i.e. a fresh random ability roll.
The static ATTRACT mode has no sim, so the animation half of this test would be vacuous.

steps.expression: (() => { const ns = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid^="splash-player-"]')]; return JSON.stringify(ns.map(n => n.getAttribute('data-team') + ' ' + n.getAttribute('data-role') + ': ' + n.getAttribute('data-abilities'))); })()
steps._comment: The actual rolled loadouts, for eyeballing the distribution.

steps.expression: (() => { document.querySelectorAll('#probe-ten,#probe-each-two,#probe-variety').forEach(n=>n.remove()); const ns = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid^="splash-player-"]')]; const lists = ns.map(n => (n.getAttribute('data-abilities')||'').split(',').filter(Boolean)); const every2 = lists.length > 0 && lists.every(l => l.length === 2 && new Set(l).size === 2); const union = new Set(lists.flat()); const mk = id => { const d = document.createElement('div'); d.id = id; document.body.appendChild(d); }; if (ns.length === 10) mk('probe-ten'); if (every2) mk('probe-each-two'); if (union.size >= 3) mk('probe-variety'); return JSON.stringify({players: ns.length, sizes: lists.map(l=>l.length), distinct: [...union]}); })()

steps._comment: ASSERTION 1: a full 5v5 is on the floor, so 'everyone' means all 10.
ASSERTION 2: every player has exactly ABILITIES_PER_PLAYER abilities and they are distinct - rollAbilities samples without replacement.
ASSERTION 3: at least 3 different abilities across the 20 draws. Guards against a degenerate roller handing the same ability to everyone (which would still satisfy assertions 1 and 2).

steps.until: (() => { window.__anims = window.__anims || {}; document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid^="splash-player-"]').forEach(n => { const a = n.getAttribute('data-anim') || 'idle'; window.__anims[a] = (window.__anims[a] || 0) + 1; }); const gated = ['spindunk','ironblock','pickpocket','fadeaway','spin','dash']; return gated.some(a => window.__anims[a] > 0); })()
steps._comment: Poll every 250ms, accumulating every animation state seen into window.__anims. Exits as soon as an ability-gated animation shows up.
Full histogram of sampled animation states - shows what the feed tile is actually rendering.

steps.expression: (() => { document.querySelectorAll('#probe-gated-anim').forEach(n=>n.remove()); const gated = ['spindunk','ironblock','pickpocket','fadeaway','spin','dash']; const seen = gated.filter(a => (window.__anims||{})[a] > 0); if (seen.length) { const d = document.createElement('div'); d.id='probe-gated-anim'; document.body.appendChild(d); } return JSON.stringify({gatedSeen: seen}); })()

steps._comment: ASSERTION 4: at least one animation that is impossible without an ability. This is the end-to-end link: roster row -> hasAbility() -> sprite.
